issues.legal_issue: Trustee remuneration calculated as a percentage of agricultural income from trust property does not retain the agricultural character of that income when the entitlement to remuneration arises from a management covenant rather than a legal or beneficial interest in the land or its income.
material_facts: A trust deed settled land and its income for maintaining religious institutions and appointed the settlor as trustee.
The trustee was entitled under the deed to remuneration calculated as a percentage of the trust properties’ net income, including income from agricultural land.
The trustee had no beneficial interest in the trust property and received the remuneration under a covenant for managing the trust.
The trustee claimed that the remuneration was exempt as agricultural income, but the tax authorities treated it as taxable.
issues.conclusion: The remuneration was not agricultural income under section 2(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, and was not exempt under section 4(3)(viii).
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, income must itself be rent or revenue derived from agricultural land to qualify as agricultural income; it does not acquire that character merely because its source is agricultural income or because it is calculated by reference to that income. The remuneration here arose from a contractual entitlement for management services, not from a legal or beneficial title to the land or its income. This applies the principles in Nawab Habibulla v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bengal, and Premier Construction Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay City. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar and Orissa v. Kameshwar Singh was distinguished because the mortgagee there received agricultural income by virtue of legal ownership and possession, and the court considered the character of the primary receipt rather than a later appropriation as remuneration. K. B. Syed Mohammad Isa was also distinguished because the mutwalli there was a beneficiary entitled to the residue of the income.

rule.if: trustee_remuneration_tax_appeal and agricultural_income_exemption_claim and remuneration_calculated_from_agricultural_trust_income and management_service_covenant and no_property_based_entitlement

predicates.trustee_remuneration_tax_appeal: The proceeding concerns the tax treatment of remuneration received by a trustee.
predicates.agricultural_income_exemption_claim: The recipient claims that the remuneration is exempt because it is agricultural income.
predicates.remuneration_calculated_from_agricultura: The remuneration is calculated by reference to income from agricultural property held in trust.
predicates.management_service_covenant: The recipient's entitlement to the remuneration arises from a covenant to manage the trust.
predicates.no_property_based_entitlement: The recipient has no legal or beneficial interest in the land or a property-based right to receive its income as remuneration.

issues.definition: When a trustee’s tax appeal concerns a claim that remuneration calculated from agricultural trust income is exempt, and the remuneration entitlement arises from a management covenant without a property-based entitlement, the remuneration is not exempt as agricultural income.
